subject.title: fix(codex): stop stale MCP child processes with revalidated SIGKILL escalation

question: Should OpenClaw adopt an automatic two-second SIGKILL fallback for stale Codex Computer Use MCP children, or should forced termination remain disabled until the Codex helper lifecycle contract is confirmed?
rationale: This changes the failure policy for an externally owned macOS helper; source-level unit tests and a Linux exercise with the platform guard overridden cannot establish the intended Codex cleanup and recovery contract.

options.title: Approve the forced-termination contract
options.body: Confirm that a two-second revalidated SIGKILL is the intended recovery policy, contingent on supported macOS app-server proof.

options.title: Keep SIGTERM-only cleanup
options.body: Retain the existing best-effort termination behavior until Codex exposes or documents a safe stale-helper shutdown contract.

options.title: Use a Codex-supported recovery seam
options.body: Replace direct force-killing with an upstream-supported app-server or helper shutdown path if one exists.

recommendation.title: Approve the forced-termination contract
recommendation.body: Confirm that a two-second revalidated SIGKILL is the intended recovery policy, contingent on supported macOS app-server proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex app-server lifecycle hardening makes steipete the strongest available routing candidate for the contract decision.
